The Faber language

Everything you need to read Faber is on this page. The pages beneath it go deeper on each part, but nothing here is a placeholder — if you read this far and stop, you can read a Faber program.

A whole program#

freader locale
faber convert --to en — English reader surface
fn saturate(int x) → int {
    if x ≺ 0 then return 0
    if x ≻ 255 then return 255
    return x
}

main {
    let int v ← saturate(300)
    print v
}
faber convert --to la — canonical Faber
functio saturate(numerus x) → numerus {
    si x ≺ 0 ergo redde 0
    si x ≻ 255 ergo redde 255
    redde x
}

incipit {
    sit numerus v ← saturate(300)
    nota v
}
faber convert --to th-TH — Thai
ฟังก์ชัน saturate(จํานวน x) → จํานวน {
    ถ้า x ≺ 0 ดังนั้น คืน 0
    ถ้า x ≻ 255 ดังนั้น คืน 255
    คืน x
}

เริ่ม {
    กำหนด จํานวน v ← saturate(300)
    บันทึก v
}
faber convert --to zh-Hans — Simplified Chinese
函数 saturate(整数 x) → 整数 {
    如果 x ≺ 0 则 返回 0
    如果 x ≻ 255 则 返回 255
    返回 x
}

入口 {
    设 整数 v ← saturate(300)
    显示 v
}
faber convert --to zh-Hant — Traditional Chinese
函式 saturate(整數 x) → 整數 {
    若 x ≺ 0 則 傳回 0
    若 x ≻ 255 則 傳回 255
    傳回 x
}

入口 {
    設為 整數 v ← saturate(300)
    註記 v
}
faber convert --to vi — Vietnamese
hàm saturate(số x) → số {
    nếu x ≺ 0 do_đó trả 0
    nếu x ≻ 255 do_đó trả 255
    trả x
}

bắt_đầu {
    đặt số v ← saturate(300)
    ghi_chú v
}
faber convert --to ar — Arabic
دالة saturate(عدد x) → عدد {
    إذا x ≺ 0 إذن أعد 0
    إذا x ≻ 255 إذن أعد 255
    أعد x
}

بداية {
    ليكن عدد v ← saturate(300)
    اعرض v
}
faber convert --to hi — Hindi
फलन saturate(संख्या x) → संख्या {
    यदि x ≺ 0 अतः लौटाओ 0
    यदि x ≻ 255 अतः लौटाओ 255
    लौटाओ x
}

आरंभ {
    बैठा संख्या v ← saturate(300)
    दिखाओ v
}

That is a complete, compilable package entry point. Reading it left to right:

PieceWhat it is
fndeclares a function
int xthe type comes before the name — always, everywhere
→ intthe return type
if … thena compact single-branch conditional
returnreturn
mainthe program entry point
leta fixed name (mut is the writable one)
←bind this value to that name
printprint

Type before name, always#

This is the single rule that makes the rest of the grammar small:

freader locale
faber convert --to en — English reader surface
main {
    # a declaration
    let int count ← 0
    # another
    let string name ← "Marcus"
    # a generic
    let list<int> scores ← [1, 2, 3]
    # a nullable
    let int ∪ none maybe ← null
    print count, name, scores, maybe
}
faber convert --to la — canonical Faber
incipit {
    # a declaration
    sit numerus count ← 0
    # another
    sit textus name ← "Marcus"
    # a generic
    sit lista<numerus> scores ← [1, 2, 3]
    # a nullable
    sit numerus ∪ nihil maybe ← nulla
    nota count, name, scores, maybe
}
faber convert --to th-TH — Thai
เริ่ม {
    # a declaration
    กำหนด จํานวน count ← 0
    # another
    กำหนด ข้อความ name ← "Marcus"
    # a generic
    กำหนด รายการ<จํานวน> scores ← [1, 2, 3]
    # a nullable
    กำหนด จํานวน ∪ ไม่มี maybe ← ขาดหาย
    บันทึก count, name, scores, maybe
}
faber convert --to zh-Hans — Simplified Chinese
入口 {
    # a declaration
    设 整数 count ← 0
    # another
    设 文本 name ← "Marcus"
    # a generic
    设 列表<整数> scores ← [1, 2, 3]
    # a nullable
    设 整数 ∪ 无 maybe ← 缺失
    显示 count, name, scores, maybe
}
faber convert --to zh-Hant — Traditional Chinese
入口 {
    # a declaration
    設為 整數 count ← 0
    # another
    設為 文字 name ← "Marcus"
    # a generic
    設為 列表<整數> scores ← [1, 2, 3]
    # a nullable
    設為 整數 ∪ 無 maybe ← 缺失
    註記 count, name, scores, maybe
}
faber convert --to vi — Vietnamese
bắt_đầu {
    # a declaration
    đặt số count ← 0
    # another
    đặt văn_bản name ← "Marcus"
    # a generic
    đặt danh_sách<số> scores ← [1, 2, 3]
    # a nullable
    đặt số ∪ hư_không maybe ← vắng
    ghi_chú count, name, scores, maybe
}
faber convert --to ar — Arabic
بداية {
    # a declaration
    ليكن عدد count ← 0
    # another
    ليكن نص name ← "Marcus"
    # a generic
    ليكن قائمة<عدد> scores ← [1, 2, 3]
    # a nullable
    ليكن عدد ∪ لاشيء maybe ← غائب
    اعرض count, name, scores, maybe
}
faber convert --to hi — Hindi
आरंभ {
    # a declaration
    बैठा संख्या count ← 0
    # another
    बैठा पाठ name ← "Marcus"
    # a generic
    बैठा सूची<संख्या> scores ← [1, 2, 3]
    # a nullable
    बैठा संख्या ∪ कुछनहीं maybe ← अभाव
    दिखाओ count, name, scores, maybe
}

There is no name: type form to learn. A declaration is a type followed by a name, whether it is a parameter, a local, or a field. Four binding words say how a name is bound: let is a fixed name, mut is re-pointable and writable, ref is re-pointable and read-only, and const is a compile-time fact set with =. Every one writes its type slot, and _ asks the compiler to infer the type. See Types and values.

Six glyphs, and what they mean#

Faber uses a small fixed set of symbols for structure. They never localize — they are the same in every reader locale, which is what keeps a program recognizable across languages.

GlyphMeaning
←bind a value to a name
→function return type
∪union type, most often T ∪ none for nullable
⇥alternate exit — the error channel
∴closure joint, connecting a signature to its body
≡equality

Two more appear when you convert between types: ∷ for a compile-time ascription and ↦ for a runtime conversion that can fail. Full table in Glyphs and Latin.

The words you write, and the compiler's Latin#

The words in the program above — fn, if, return, let, int — are the spellings an English reader writes; every page on this site teaches the English reader surface. Latin is one reader locale like the rest; the pack files are keyed by Latin spellings, so the grammar document prints its Latin identity rendering beside the others. faber convert --to la prints any program in Latin, and reader locales render the same program in seven other languages. The glyphs and the type-first shape survive every rendering untouched — and identifiers like saturate are never translated.
